title: History Record v1
description: One terminal record of one exit, in ANY of the three append-only history ledgers (specs/backlog/_archive/backlog_histo.jsonl, specs/audits/_archive/audits_histo.jsonl, specs/releases/_archive/releases_histo.jsonl) — release 0.4.7 FR7. Before this schema the three files had three hand-written shapes, no schema and no reader: two were event streams wrapping a free-form 'data' object, so a history record could not be validated at all. ONE shape for all three: 'id'/'ts'/'disposition' are the immutable core (identity and terminal verdict), 'release'/'reason'/'summary' are nullable free text, 'entry' is the removed object itself (the backlog entry, the audit's per-pillar counts) or null when the exit had nothing to snapshot. The per-ledger terminal vocabulary is a PARAMETER of the validator (which of the five words this ledger may use — backlog: delivered/superseded/rejected; audits: resolved/superseded/deferred/rejected; releases: delivered), never a second or third schema file.

id.description: The exiting subject's own stable identity — the backlog slug, the audit directory name, the release id. One line per id, ever.

ts.description: When the exit happened: an ISO-8601 date or UTC timestamp. Date-only values are accepted because migrated pre-0.4.7 records carry them.

disposition.description: The terminal verdict, from the ONE lowercase vocabulary (core.models.histo.TERMINAL_DISPOSITIONS). Each ledger is validated against its own subset of these five words.

release.description: The release that dispositioned this subject, or null when none did.

reason.description: Why this disposition, when the disposition alone does not say it.

summary.description: One-paragraph narrative of the exit: what shipped, what the audit measured, what a note said before the event wrapper was removed.

entry.description: The removed object itself — the backlog active[] entry, the audit's window-end sha and per-pillar counts — or null.

examples.summary: Shipped as the pre-push whole-tree denylist scan.
